question_asked: Does the demo reach a candidate Part B and a blind baseline: Phase 8 released or its blocking gate recorded; candidate version 1 imported as a document snapshot with passages linked by span; a blind report carrying the candidate hash, profile version and assessor pin; and the leakage guard confirming no historical-feedback item entered the package?
answer: Four of four. Criterion 1 is met on its first branch: all six Phase 8 nodes are released and gate_12 passed 14 of 14 predicates. Criterion 2 is met: candidate version 1 is imported as a document snapshot with state 'imported' and its passages linked by span. Criterion 3 is met: the operator ran the assessor over the Max subscription and the report carries the candidate hash, the profile version and the assessor pin on its header and on each of its six cells, labelled scope 'complete'. Criterion 4 is met over the package the criterion names, which holds 151 items and so can carry the leak the guard looks for. The ticket closes. The grades themselves are advisory: two cells of six are a clean pass, and the single systematic reason the other four are not is F12, a traceability break between the candidate converter and the materialiser that no gate caught and the blind assessor did.

the_esr_intake.why_not_applicable: The demo is a demonstration, not a submission. Nothing was submitted, so no Evaluation Summary Report exists and none can. not_applicable states that, where unavailable would state that a report exists and was not obtained. The intake module declares availability and never infers it, so the field had to be set explicitly: prior_submission false on its own would have stored unknown.
the_esr_intake.why_it_is_written_now: Writing the intake is not Phase 8 activity. §13.4 covers the Phase 8 substeps — drafting, assembly, evaluator review, revision — and this is an out-of-band dev-graph record of what is known about an ESR. It fixes the document identity the eventual import must use, which is what makes that import checkable rather than negotiable. The builder never reads the intake directory, so the demo snapshot id is unchanged at sha256:93b18297a8703157e77e08d1a3c97abd240f752b63b711ca0b3037f6141bd836. Candidate version 1 moved it on 2 October, from that id to sha256:706fe54fd85ebda600d70b02c80ce6ca1e12e2697b373a45cf730ef03504e389, because importing a document adds an artifact_version node, three passages and 147 claims. The intake record is still not a graph record and still moves nothing.
the_esr_intake.cost_of_writing_it_early: An intake record is immutable. If Phase 8 later produces Part B under a document id other than DEMO-BIODIV-2027_part_b, this record is wrong and a new intake id is required. The id follows the demo project label the snapshot summary already carries, which is the only project identity this branch has: the acronym in Tier 3 is Unresolved.

findings.severity: blocking for the blind lane's guarded route
findings.finding: The dev-graph document route cannot feed either real instrument profile. materialise_candidate writes one sub-section per passage and gives it the section's own id; the RIA rubrics anchor on B.1.1, B.1.2, B.2.1, B.2.2, B.3.1 and B.3.2, and the MSCA-PF rubrics on 1.1 to 3.2. build_evidence_pack fails closed on the missing anchor. The only profile the route can serve is one whose rubric anchors equal its section ids, which describes the synthetic syn_graph profile in tests/harness/test_blind_leakage.py and no shipped profile.
findings.why_it_was_not_caught_before: The document route's tests use the synthetic profile, where anchor and section id coincide. The RIA and MSCA-PF profile tests use the directory route with a candidate built from the rubric anchors. No test crossed the two. This is what handoff stage 7 was for.
findings.disposition: FIXED by ticket B on 2026-10-01. A document section carries an optional sub_sections list; the builder copies it onto the passage node and materialise_candidate emits it instead of synthesising one. The field is optional and an empty list normalises to absent, so no record's content_version moves. The anchor map still fails closed: a document declaring no sub-section, or declaring fewer than the profile anchors on, still raises. Proved by tests/harness/test_blind_document_subsections.py (22 tests).
findings.fix_shape: Either a document record declares its sub-sections and materialise_candidate preserves them, or the profile declares how a section's passage maps onto its anchors. The first keeps the anchor map fail-closed and puts the structure where the drafter already knows it; the second changes no document schema. The choice is not this ticket's to make: it changes what a document snapshot is.

findings.finding: An ESR intake can be stamped on a blind report only through the document route: _check_intake refuses an intake when the candidate is a directory, because a directory names no document. While F1 stands, the demo's not_applicable availability cannot reach any RIA blind report, so criteria 3 and 4 cannot be satisfied by the same report.
findings.disposition: FIXED with F1 by ticket B. An ESR intake now stamps onto a report produced through the document route, and demo-biodiv-2027-part-b-v1 is the record it was proved with.
findings.fix_shape: None of its own. Fixing F1 resolves it.

findings.finding: record_esr_intake requires a submission_id matching a plain-identifier pattern, with no way to declare that no submission exists. The demo was never submitted and never will be, so the record carries the sentinel NOT_SUBMITTED. The sentinel is a declaration of absence, not an invented identifier, and cannot be mistaken for a submission number.
findings.fix_shape: Make submission_id optional when esr_availability is not_applicable, or add a declared absence value. Either way it stays declared and never inferred, which is the module's existing rule.

findings.finding: Phase 8 has produced nothing, so there is no candidate version 1. This is the gate working, not a defect. The outstanding step is the operator's: run the external planner and place the response in received/.

The demo world's 6 blind packages hold no passage, claim or commitment item: the item types are task 50, participant 22, work_package 6, source 4 and deliverable 2. The builder derives those three types from document records, and the demo has none. A historical-feedback tag is stamped on a document's passages, claims and commitments, so no item in these packages could carry one. assert_no_leakage passing over them is correct and tells a reader nothing about whether a real Part B package would be clean.
findings.disposition: recorded; it is why criterion 4's box stays open
findings.fix_shape: None at the code level. The check becomes meaningful when a document record exists, which is criterion 2.

findings.finding: The demo's 6 blind packages are all labelled incomplete under the budget of 3000 that ticket 8 used. assert_no_leakage is indifferent to completeness, but build_blind_evidence refuses an incomplete package outright, so the budget a real Part B assessment needs is higher than the one the snapshot ticket demonstrated with. Ticket 8 recorded 5.4k to 21.9k for the mandatory set, and the blind lane's own default package budget is 200000.
findings.disposition: recorded; no change made, because no real package is built yet

findings.finding: The candidate builder had no mapping for an 'assumed' claim, so it refused the real Part B outright. CLAUDE.md section 12.2 defines four status categories and the builder's EVIDENCE_STRENGTH_BY_STATUS covered three. The omission is not an oversight in the lookup: the graph has no evidence_strength that yields Assumed, because Assumed is declared rather than evidenced. normalise_candidate admits exactly one override for this — 'only Assumed over Unresolved may be declared' — mirroring the flip assumption_applier makes. Carrying an assumed claim on strength alone would have landed it as Unresolved and silently discarded the operator declaration. The demo's Part B carries 85 such claims out of 180.
findings.disposition: FIXED. The builder maps 'assumed' to the 'unconfirmed' strength and declares 'Assumed' alongside it, through DECLARED_STATUS_BY_STATUS. Every other status is still derived by the graph. The declaration survives into the blind assessor's ledger: 11, 17 and 24 assumed claims reach the three materialised sections.

findings.finding: Two counting defects, found by converting a real Part B. First, a Tier 5 claim_id is a declaration key, not an occurrence id. All three sections assert project_duration, and the section assembler concatenates the per-sub-section ledgers without deduplicating, so one declaration arrives up to six times in one section with an identical status and summary. 180 ledger entries carry 122 distinct ids. A graph claim node belongs to one section and its id is unique across the document, so the identity is the pair. Second, the demo dev-graph builder never prunes: a snapshot shift leaves the previous generation's package directories on disk, so 54 directories now hold 18 current packages. The 1 October evidence for criterion 4 counted 36 directories and 6 blind packages, of which 18 and 3 belonged to a superseded snapshot.
findings.disposition: The first half is FIXED: the builder scopes each claim id to its section, collapses an exact repeat, and refuses a repeat that disagrees rather than picking a side (section 12.3). 180 entries become 147 claims. The second half is recorded unfixed and offered as a Milestone 2 candidate: pruning a superseded generation deletes records that cannot be rebuilt, which is the operator's call and not this act's.

findings.finding: One provider's free-tier rate limit was deciding how much of the Part B the assessor is allowed to read. MAX_PACK_TOKEN_BUDGET was defined as GROQ_TPM_LIMIT - DEFAULT_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS - RUBRIC_PROMPT_ALLOWANCE = 6000 - 2048 - 900 = 3052, and build_evidence_pack refused any larger budget outright. Measured over the six candidate packs at the shipped default of 3000, that cap drops 111 of 266 relevant items and truncates every single cell; the implementation workplan cell loses 32 of its 53. The rubric system prompt then tells the assessor that a pack marked insufficient_context means 'you must not return passed: true'. Every grade in the report was therefore predetermined before any model read anything, and the report would have measured the rate limit rather than the proposal. The number is a property of the assessor's transport, not of the proposal or of the harness.
findings.disposition: FIXED. The ceiling is now a parameter, max_token_budget, threaded through build_evidence_pack, build_pack_for, grade_expectation and assess_candidate. It still defaults to MAX_PACK_TOKEN_BUDGET, so every existing caller and the whole Groq lane are byte-for-byte unchanged; a transport with no per-minute token ceiling passes None, and then the operator's --budget alone governs. Lifting the ceiling does not lift the floor: a budget that is still too small reports insufficient_context exactly as before, and is never silently stretched to make a pack fit. The smallest budget at which all six candidate packs complete is 10501, bisected rather than estimated; UNCAPPED_DEFAULT_PACK_TOKEN_BUDGET is 32768, a chosen constant whose basis is that measurement plus roughly threefold headroom.

findings.finding: A rejected API key printed a traceback instead of failing closed. blind_assessment's main converts a closed set of errors to exit code 2 with one readable line, and no transport error was in that set, so the 401 propagated out of assess_candidate through runpy and the operator read a twelve-frame stack trace for a configuration problem. The module docstring describes the command as fail-closed throughout.
findings.disposition: FIXED. A transport failure on either transport now prints one line and returns exit 2, like every other fail-closed condition. The check is lazy, so importing the command still pulls in neither transport, and it re-raises anything that is not a transport error rather than swallowing it. SubscriptionJudgeError was additionally made a JudgeError so a mismatched assessor pin lands in the same path.

findings.finding: Three real-data probes in tests/harness/test_evidence_pack.py (TestRealSections) fail on this branch, and they failed before this act. They read docs/tier5_deliverables/proposal_sections/ with the harness default rubrics, whose anchors are the MSCA-PF spelling '1.1', while Phase 8 wrote RIA sections declaring 'B.1.1' and 'B.1.2'. The anchor map fails closed, which is correct behaviour meeting a probe that hardcodes one instrument's spelling. The same mismatch is the F1 that ticket B fixed for the document route; the direct-section route still carries it in its test fixtures.
findings.disposition: OPEN, and out of this ticket's scope. A Milestone 2 candidate: the probe should resolve its anchors from the profile that matches the sections on disk, rather than assuming MSCA-PF. Recorded here so the three failures are not read as a regression from this act.

findings.finding: Every claim reaches the assessor with no source. All 147 claims in the candidate carry source_ref '', including the 90 declared 'confirmed', and the assessor named this in all six cells unprompted: 'every ledger entry carries an empty source_ref'. Upstream the field is intact. The three Tier 5 sections hold 180 claim_statuses entries and not one is blank; excellence_section's first is docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding/selected_call.json. The break is a seam between two components that are each correct alone. tools/build_part_b_candidate.py::_claims maps claim_id, status and claim_summary onto the graph's claim shape and does not carry source_ref; its docstring explains, correctly, that it leaves verified_span absent because inventing offsets would defeat the claim verifier. harness/blind_assessment.py::materialise_candidate then derives source_ref from verified_span['id'] alone, which is the one field the converter deliberately never writes, so it resolves to ''. The harness is faithful throughout: evidence_pack renders the field verbatim as 'source_ref=' and the assessor judged what it was shown. Under CLAUDE.md 12.2 a 'confirmed' claim is one directly evidenced by a named source in Tier 1-3; in the candidate the name is gone, so the candidate understates its own traceability against a Tier 5 state that has it.
findings.disposition: OPEN, and out of this ticket's scope. The criterion asks what the report binds and how it is labelled, and the report binds and labels correctly. A Milestone 2 candidate, and the first finding on this branch produced by the blind assessor rather than by a deterministic check: no gate caught it, because every component passed its own contract. The fix is to carry the Tier 5 source_ref through the converter into the graph claim, and to have materialise_candidate prefer it over the absent verified_span rather than fall back to ''. Until then, every grounding judgment in a blind report on this route is made against a blank field and understates the candidate.

findings.finding: The two implementation cells score lowest, at 0.323 and 0.283, and the assessor's reasoning is that the load-bearing figures are not grounded: every person-month in Tables 3.1a and 3.1f reads 'not agreed' or 'TBD', the resources are deferred to a future lump-sum response, the risk register is flagged assumed, and all twelve partner_participation entries are assumed. That is not a defect in the draft. It is the demo's Tier 3 being almost entirely Assumed by construction, which ticket 4 recorded and 13.8 required the sections to concede, and the sections do concede it, in the prose the assessor quotes back: 'Every partner's participation is an operator assumption'.
findings.disposition: NOT A DEFECT, recorded so the scores are not read as one. The blind assessor priced an all-Assumed Tier 3 at roughly 0.3 on implementation and the drafts told it so plainly, which is the lane working. A real project would close these by confirming the consortium and receiving the budget; the fictional one cannot and must not.
